lines.text: Hi, I'm Clawd! Twelve thousand years ago, nobody on Earth was a farmer. So how did we start growing our food?
Meet Ana. She lives in the Fertile Crescent, in the Middle East, where wild wheat and barley grow on the hills.
Like everyone back then, Ana's family moves with the seasons. They hunt gazelle, and gather nuts, berries and wild grain.
But wild wheat has a trick. When it's ripe, the seeds shatter, and fall to the ground. You have to be quick.
A few rare plants are different. Their seeds stay stuck on the stalk. They're the easiest to harvest, so those are the ones that go home in the basket.
Some of those seeds get dropped, or planted, near camp. Next spring, they come up again, right where people live.
Generation after generation, people keep sowing seed from the best plants. Slowly, the wheat changes. Its seeds stay on, and grow bigger. It's becoming a crop.
Fields need looking after, so people stay put. Tents become mud-brick houses, and houses become villages, like Jericho.
Sheep and goats are tamed too. Now there's food to store, and more mouths to feed.
And it didn't happen just once. People invented farming again and again: rice and millet in China, maize in Mexico, potatoes in the Andes, sorghum in Africa.
Farming changed everything. Towns, trade, writing, cities. It all started with a few seeds that didn't fall.
See you in the next story!
